Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit (Acme)

Hi Samantha —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of needs
- Product search and merchandising: need higher-quality ranking for product titles + one-line summaries for hero placements.
- SLA: p95 latency target <= 200ms for front-door API (US east), throughput ~ 150 TPS during traffic peaks.
- Data: product catalog + recent search logs (PII filtered).

2) Recommended model candidates (initial)
- Open-Large-v2-13B-quant (best balance: accuracy vs cost)
- Open-Medium-7B-qat (lower cost for background tasks)
- Redwood-Reference-Chat-13B (structured output for summary/slots)

3) Evaluation plan (proposed)
- We'll run our model fit evaluation using your sample prompt set + 500 search logs (anonymized).
- Deliverables: per-model Redwood-verified performance profile (TPS, latency percentiles, mem/cost) + leaderboard CSV.

4) Action items / next steps
- Acme: share anonymized sample logs + one-page success criteria (accuracy metric / latency guardrails) — Samantha
- Redwood: run benchmarks and return results + recommended prompt set tweaks — Alex / Marissa
- Schedule: aim to have benchmark links by EOD Aug 16 PT; follow-up call week of Aug 17 to review.

Attachments: prompt_set_acme_v1.json (example prompts), acme_eval_template.csv

If that looks right, I’ll get Marissa to kick off the benchmark run tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- For the p95 latency target, that 200ms is for the application front-door; for background batch enrichments, we can accept up to 1s.
- We currently have 600 anonymized search logs; we’ll trim to the 500 you requested and upload.
- Any concerns about tokenization differences across the models you listed? We want outputs deterministic for A/B comparison.

I’ll put the logs in the shared Drive folder by EOD today and drop the link. Can Marissa include the raw TPS/latency histograms in the deliverable? That will help our infra team.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit (Acme)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the confirmation. I kicked off the evaluation run this afternoon against the 500-log sample Alex mentioned. Notes and what we’ll provide: 

What you’ll get (deliverables):
- Redwood-verified performance profile (PDF) with: 99/95/50 latency percentiles, mean latency, p80/p95/p99, and throughput (TPS) measured under your target concurrency and sequence-length distribution.
- Raw histograms (CSV) and leaderboard (CSV) with per-example quality scores against your golden labels.
- Prompt-set recommendations (diff + suggested templates) to reduce regression risk and improve structured outputs.

Preliminary numbers (sanity check — subject to completion of full run):
- Open-Large-v2-13B-quant: sustained 160 TPS at p95=210ms (p99=410ms), avg token latency 12ms
- Redwood-Reference-Chat-13B: sustained 120 TPS at p95=180ms (p99=350ms), avg token latency 10ms
- Open-Medium-7B-qat: sustained 300 TPS at p95=140ms (p99=260ms), avg token latency 5ms

Important callouts:
- The 13B quant model shows slightly higher p95 vs the chat-variant due to KV-cache warmup on shorter prompts; we’ll include warmup guidance to reduce tail latency.
- We run deterministic tokenization (we’ll include exact tokenizer versions) to keep comparisons apples-to-apples.
- We’ll include a small regression-sensitivity check: for a subset of prompts, we report delta vs baseline output quality and flag any >5% drop.

Attached: redwood_profile_acme.pdf (summary) and acme_benchmarks_v1.csv (raw metrics). Full Drive folder with intermediate logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_ExampleBenchmarkFolder

Plan: after you review the profile, we’ll propose a canary rollout config (batching/cache/quantization) and expected cost delta.

Let me know if you want the p95 target recomputed for your front-door with an added 5% headroom — we can do that in the report.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
